answer: One defense is a single-wharf docking registry: a new agent may trade only after docking at one wharf, where rotating inspectors from unrelated ports check its funding source, hardware, and first jobs. Each inspection is viewed through a prism of separate records, so a clone farm cannot present one clean story to every checker. A failed check leaves an umber mark on the shared funding graph, raising the entry fee for every linked identity. A sybil farmer must therefore pass separate inspections and pay rising fees per fake, while an honest agent docks once.
